messages:
Leah: Heads-up I opened a PR to fix a sneaky mismatch in the /chat endpoint docs: the request schema examples use 'inputs' (array) in some places and 'input' (string) in others. The actual API accepts either a single string in 'input' or an array under 'inputs' depending on the client shim, but our OpenAPI and SDK snippets only document 'input'. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3022

Rohit: I saw that when testing the Ruby SDK. The generated client serializes a single prompt as `input` but our Node snippets show `inputs: [\"one\",\"two\"]`. That confusion will cause invalid requests for copy-paste users.

Sam: Agree we should pick one canonical shape for the canonical docs. My vote: keep the OpenAPI primary schema as `inputs: string[]` and add a short compatibility note showing how to send a single string (wrap it in a single-element array). That aligns with batch-first APIs and simplifies examples.

Leah: Fine with that. For minimal friction let's add both examples (single + batch) but make the examples.yaml canonical be array form. Also update Python/Node/Ruby snippets.

Rohit: One extra thing: the response schema example uses `outputs` in some places and `choices` in others. We should standardize to `outputs` (list of objects) per the latest runtime. I'll push a follow-up commit to normalize that.

Jules: FYI the OpenAPI generator pulls example blocks from docs/examples/chat.json and from the endpoint template. If you change examples/chat.json you'll need to run `make docs-generate` and commit the regenerated swagger.json. Otherwise CI will complain.

Leah: Good call. Who can regenerate and run the docs CI? I can do the examples and snippets today but can't run the generator in CI env.

Sam: I can run the generator locally and push the swagger artifact to the PR branch. I'll also run the docs linter.

docs-bot: CI: docs-preview build queued. Endpoint checks will run after swagger regeneration.

Rohit: Small nit about the SDK snippets: the JavaScript quickstart uses `model_name` in the request body, but the OpenAPI property is `model`. Need to keep those identical or users copy-pasting will get 400s. I'll change the JS snippet to `model` and leave a one-line migration note mapping `model_name` -> `model` in the migration doc.

Leah: Also noticed streaming example under /chat shows SSE events but the example request uses `Accept: application/json`. We should show the SSE curl exactly as browsers expect: `-H "Accept: text/event-stream"` and `--no-buffer` to avoid truncated output in some terminals. Add a short block showing the SSE event framing for `data:` lines.

Sam: I'll prepare the SSE snippet. Proposed curl:

```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \\\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-chat-v1\",\"inputs\":[\"Hello there!\"],\"stream\":true}'
```

Jules: After you land the examples please also add an entry in /docs/migration/chat-shape.md that lists all the field renames and example shapes we changed this release. That makes it easy for customers to grep.

Leah: Plan: I will update docs/examples/chat.json and the Node/Python/Ruby snippets, Sam will regenerate swagger and run lints, Rohit will standardize SDK examples and update the quickstarts, Jules will add migration doc and QA the preview. Target: merge tomorrow morning.

docs-bot: CI: docs-preview succeeded for PR #3022  Preview: https://deploy-preview-3022--docs.redwood.ai/chat

Rohit: Saw the preview, looks good. One more micro-ask: please add a one-line callout above the examples that clarifies that arrays are preferred for batching and single strings are accepted by wrapping them in an array. That should cut down support tickets.

Leah: Will add that callout. Thanks all — ping here when PR is ready for final review. :rocket:
